title: LHD Cycle Evaluation
body: When nobody breaks the load-haul-dump cycle into its five stages, slow fill times and bucket hang-ups hide inside the daily tonnage number until they've cost a shift's worth of production — like the Oct 6 EX262 check, where every truck's bucket time ran over benchmark and nobody caught it until someone stood at the viewpoint with a stopwatch.
keyPoints: Five stages, always: load, haul loaded, dump, return empty, idle. If you can't say which one is bleeding time, you're guessing at the fix.
The daily workbooks give aggregate output, not per-stage breakdown — the only way to find the real bottleneck is direct observation at the face or the dump.
Operator variability is the single biggest lever from the Kaizen work — same machine, same face, different operators, different cycle times. That's a training fix, not an equipment fix.
Fragmentation, face height, and loader positioning at the loading phase set the ceiling for everything downstream — bad blast rock slows fill time no matter how good the operator is.

A breakdown pattern often shows up first as recurring delay-reason codes before it shows up as a full stoppage — if a unit keeps logging the same hydraulic or final-drive flag, that's your early warning, not the eventual down day.
apply: Pick one truck-excavator pair on your face and time three cycles against the 4.0 min fill / 32 s bucket benchmark — if you're running long like EX262 did on Oct 6, that's volume walking out the door before the shift even ends.
